The application of risk treatment options does not need to be mutually exclusive. A risk owner is likely to apply a hybrid of multiple treatment options to achieve the desired effect. The goal of the risk owner is to evaluate the options that will best achieve the balance among value, risk, and resources.", "bbox": [ 184, 676, 872, 793 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "For any of the options selected, recommendations on how to proceed with the selected option have to be made to management. Besides, safeguards and security controls have to be suggested if it is decided to reduce risk.", "bbox": [ 186, 807, 860, 859 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "If no treatment options are available or treatment options do not sufficiently modify the risk, the risk should be recorded and kept under ongoing review.", "bbox": [ 186, 872, 870, 908 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "header", "text": "Security Risk Assessment", "bbox": [ 665, 57, 880, 72 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Security Risk Assessment and Audit", "bbox": [ 117, 941, 571, 958 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "38", "bbox": [ 857, 942, 880, 958 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Risk owners and other stakeholders should be aware of the nature and extent of the remaining risk after risk treatment. The remaining risk should be documented and subjected to monitoring, review and further treatment where appropriate.", "bbox": [ 184, 105, 865, 156 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "4.4.4.2 Preparing and Implementing Risk Treatment Plans", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 187, 673, 208 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The purpose of risk treatment plans is to specify how the chosen treatment options will be implemented so that arrangements are understood by those involved, and progress against the plan can be monitored. The treatment plan should identify how risk treatment should be implemented.", "bbox": [ 184, 227, 868, 293 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The information provided in the treatment plan should include:", "bbox": [ 186, 309, 704, 326 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "the rationale for the selection of the treatment options, including the expected benefits to be gained;", "bbox": [ 191, 342, 855, 375 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• those who are accountable and responsible for approving and implementing the plan;", "bbox": [ 191, 380, 870, 413 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• the proposed actions;", "bbox": [ 193, 418, 401, 435 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• the resources required, including contingencies;", "bbox": [ 191, 438, 616, 456 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• the performance measures;", "bbox": [ 193, 461, 448, 476 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• the constraints;", "bbox": [ 193, 481, 352, 497 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• the required reporting and monitoring;", "bbox": [ 191, 501, 541, 519 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• when actions are expected to be undertaken and completed.", "bbox": [ 191, 521, 709, 539 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "4.4.4.3 Residual Risk", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 575, 326, 594 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "After the implementation of risk treatment plans, residual risks may remain. These risks exist even after all planned treatment measures have been applied. It is important to manage and document these residual risks in the risk register appropriately to ensure that they do not exceed the B/D’s risk tolerance:", "bbox": [ 184, 614, 862, 682 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Regularly monitor and review residual risks. This involves tracking changes in the risk landscape, reviewing the effectiveness of the risk treatment measures, and updating risk information accordingly.", "bbox": [ 191, 696, 865, 749 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "If a residual risk is deemed too high according to the B/D’s risk tolerance, further risk treatment measures should be considered. This could include additional risk mitigation strategies or, in some cases, the decision to accept the risk if it is within the acceptable threshold but still requires monitoring.", "bbox": [ 191, 763, 873, 831 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "header", "text": "Security Risk Assessment", "bbox": [ 665, 57, 880, 72 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Security Risk Assessment and Audit", "bbox": [ 115, 941, 571, 958 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "39", "bbox": [ 857, 942, 880, 957 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "4.4.4.4 Common Types of Safeguards", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 89, 482, 109 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Safeguards can be quick fixes for problems found on existing system configurations or planned enhancements. Safeguards can be technical or procedural controls.", "bbox": [ 184, 131, 873, 166 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "In general, safeguards can be classified into three common types:", "bbox": [ 186, 187, 721, 205 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Barriers: keep unauthorised parties completely away from accessing critical resources.", "bbox": [ 186, 229, 842, 261 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Hardening: make unauthorised parties difficult to gain access to critical resources.", "bbox": [ 186, 267, 806, 299 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Monitoring: help to detect and respond to an attack promptly and correctly.", "bbox": [ 186, 304, 836, 322 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Examples of safeguards:", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 186, 343, 393, 361 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Develop/enhance the departmental IT security policy, guidelines or procedures to ensure effective security.", "bbox": [ 186, 385, 867, 418 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Re-configure operating systems, network components and devices to cater for the weaknesses identified during the security risk assessment.", "bbox": [ 186, 422, 860, 455 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Implement password control procedures or authentication mechanism to ensure strong passwords.", "bbox": [ 186, 460, 872, 493 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Implement encryption or authentication technology to protect data transmission.", "bbox": [ 186, 498, 875, 514 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Enhance physical security protection.", "bbox": [ 186, 518, 532, 535 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Develop security incident handling and reporting procedures.", "bbox": [ 186, 539, 724, 556 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Develop staff awareness and training programs to ensure compliance with security requirements.", "bbox": [ 186, 560, 828, 594 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "4.4.4.5 Major Steps of Identifying & Selecting Safeguards", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 637, 673, 657 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The selection of appropriate security safeguards is not simple. It requires knowledge and technical skills on the system. The cost of managing risks needs to commensurate with the risk exposure. That is, the cost of reducing risk on a specific asset should not exceed the total value of that asset.", "bbox": [ 184, 678, 878, 746 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Listed below are several major steps of identifying and selecting safeguards:", "bbox": [ 186, 768, 811, 785 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Select appropriate safeguards for each targeted vulnerability.", "bbox": [ 186, 809, 721, 826 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Identify the costs associated with each safeguard such as the development, implementation and maintenance costs.", "bbox": [ 186, 829, 831, 864 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Match safeguard/vulnerability pairs to all threats, i.e. develop a relationship between these measures and the threats.", "bbox": [ 186, 868, 842, 901 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "header", "text": "Security Risk Assessment", "bbox": [ 665, 57, 880, 72 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "40", "bbox": [ 855, 942, 880, 957 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Security Risk Assessment and Audit", "bbox": [ 117, 941, 571, 958 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Determine and quantify the impact of the safeguard, i.e. the extent of risk that can be reduced after applying the selected safeguards.", "bbox": [ 186, 90, 858, 124 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Different combinations of physical, managerial, procedural, operational and technical based safeguards may be required. An analysis may be required to determine the optimal combinations for different circumstances.", "bbox": [ 184, 146, 813, 197 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "A single safeguard may reduce risk for a number of threats. Several numbers of safeguards may act to reduce risk for only one threat. Hence, the integration of all safeguards shows the overall gross risk reduction benefit as a whole.", "bbox": [ 186, 219, 860, 271 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The effects of using different safeguards should be tested before implementation. Hence, this selection process may need to be performed several times to see how the proposed changes affect the risk results.", "bbox": [ 184, 291, 877, 344 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "However, there are also other factors that have to be considered other than those identified in security risk assessment.", "bbox": [ 186, 365, 843, 399 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "For example,", "bbox": [ 186, 420, 302, 439 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Organisational factors like department's goals and objectives.", "bbox": [ 186, 462, 724, 479 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Relevant statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements.", "bbox": [ 186, 483, 714, 500 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Cultural factors such as social custom, beliefs, working styles.", "bbox": [ 186, 504, 732, 520 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Quality requirements such as safety, reliability, system performance.", "bbox": [ 186, 525, 784, 542 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Time constraints.", "bbox": [ 188, 546, 369, 562 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Supporting services and functions.", "bbox": [ 186, 567, 509, 583 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Technical, procedural and operational requirements and controls.", "bbox": [ 186, 588, 754, 605 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Existing technology available in the market.", "bbox": [ 186, 609, 586, 626 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "4.4.5 Monitoring and Implementation", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 662, 497, 682 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Risk assessment results should be properly documented. This enables the security risk assessment process to be audited. This also facilitates on-going monitoring and reviewing.", "bbox": [ 184, 701, 873, 752 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Re-assessment should be conducted whenever necessary. It is essential to keep track of the changing environment and the changing priority of the identified risks and their impact. Security audit is one of the ways to review the implementation of security measures.", "bbox": [ 184, 766, 880, 834 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Roles and responsibilities of related personnel such as operators, system developers, network administrators, information owners, IT security officers and users should be clearly defined, reviewed and assigned to support the safeguard implementation.", "bbox": [ 184, 848, 878, 900 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "header", "text": "Security Risk Assessment", "bbox": [ 665, 57, 880, 72 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "41", "bbox": [ 855, 942, 878, 957 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Security Risk Assessment and Audit", "bbox": [ 115, 941, 571, 958 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Management should commit resources and provide support to monitoring and controlling the implementation.", "bbox": [ 184, 89, 823, 123 ], "page_idx": 46 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The findings from the assessment should be transferred and documented in the system risk register. This ensures that all identified risks and their corresponding mitigation strategies are accounted for in a centralised and accessible location.", "bbox": [ 186, 137, 852, 190 ], "page_idx": 46 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Establishing system level risk registers for each system is an essential practice for effective IT security risk management. These risks can then be documented in the system level risk register, providing a detailed picture of the unique risk landscape for that particular system.", "bbox": [ 186, 204, 860, 271 ], "page_idx": 46 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds shall maintain system risk registers for their systems. This register shall document at least all identified risks, their potential impacts, the likelihood of occurrence, and the corresponding risk treatment option. It serves as a comprehensive record of the B/D’s risk landscape at the system level, enabling effective monitoring, management, and communication of risks.", "bbox": [ 186, 285, 831, 370 ], "page_idx": 46 }, { "type": "text", "text": "It's important to keep the system level risk register up to date, reflecting any changes in the system's risk landscape as well as the progress of risk treatment activities. This will ensure that the register remains a useful and accurate tool for understanding and managing system-specific risks.", "bbox": [ 184, 385, 880, 453 ], "page_idx": 46 }, { "type": "text", "text": "A key part of effectively maintaining and utilising a system level risk register involves risk communication. It is importance to effectively communicate the information in the system risk register to DITSO, the risk owner and the system owner. This includes sharing the register with them in system security risk management. Clear and concise communication about risks and their risk treatment option is crucial. Transparent communication can foster a broader understanding of risks and promote collaborative efforts towards risk management.", "bbox": [ 184, 466, 873, 583 ], "page_idx": 46 }, { "type": "table", "img_path": "images/07570e19e3853d74027bbc33a5dfe5482cb15937ecb867ea4735e91e82a72095.jpg", "table_caption": [ "Figure 4.5 Example of Risk Register Template" ], "table_footnote": [], "table_body": "

Security Audit", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 99, 342, 120 ], "page_idx": 48 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Security Audit is an audit on the level of compliance with the security policy or standards as a basis to determine the overall state of the existing protection and to verify whether the existing protection has been performed properly. It targets at finding out whether the current environment is securely protected in accordance with the defined security policy. It should be performed periodically to ensure the compliance of the security policies and effective implementation of security measures.", "bbox": [ 184, 142, 882, 259 ], "page_idx": 48 }, { "type": "text", "text": "A security audit will require security policy and standards, audit checklists and an inventory list, which may cover different areas such as web application, network architecture, wireless communication, etc. Annex C lists different sample audit areas. Annex D provides a sample audit checklist under different security areas. Annex E provides a sample list of documented information as supporting evidence. Security audit may also involve the use of different auditing tools and different review techniques in order to reveal the security non-compliance and loopholes. After the audit process, an audit report will be prepared to highlight the conformance and gaps between the current protection and the requirements specified in the security policies and guidelines.", "bbox": [ 184, 280, 880, 447 ], "page_idx": 48 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The selection of auditors and conduct of audits shall ensure objectivity and impartiality of the audit process. As a general principle, auditors shall not audit their own work. System related documentation could be reviewed by the security auditor for any insufficiency or non-conformance.", "bbox": [ 184, 468, 882, 536 ], "page_idx": 48 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds should select an independent auditor not involved in the B/D’s daily operations or system development processes. This ensures the auditor can offer an unbiased assessment of the system's security posture. The selected auditor should possess relevant professional qualifications, such as Certified Information Security Professional (CISP), Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA) or Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP). These certifications indicate that the auditor has the necessary knowledge and experience to conduct thorough and effective security audits.", "bbox": [ 184, 557, 880, 690 ], "page_idx": 48 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The major objectives of a security audit are to:", "bbox": [ 186, 712, 571, 730 ], "page_idx": 48 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Check for compliance against the government security requirements based on objective evidence and inspection with existing security policy, standards, guidelines and procedures.", "bbox": [ 186, 753, 858, 804 ], "page_idx": 48 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Identify the inadequacies and examine the effectiveness of the existing policy, standards, guidelines and procedures.", "bbox": [ 186, 807, 862, 840 ], "page_idx": 48 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Identify and review relevant statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements.", "bbox": [ 186, 845, 870, 862 ], "page_idx": 48 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Identify, analyse and understand the existing vulnerabilities.", "bbox": [ 186, 865, 715, 883 ], "page_idx": 48 }, { "type": "header", "text": "Security Audit", "bbox": [ 756, 57, 880, 72 ], "page_idx": 48 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Security Risk Assessment and Audit", "bbox": [ 115, 942, 571, 958 ], "page_idx": 48 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "44", "bbox": [ 855, 942, 880, 957 ], "page_idx": 48 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Review existing security controls on operational, administrative and managerial issues, ensure effective implementation of security measures and compliance to minimum security standards.", "bbox": [ 186, 90, 875, 140 ], "page_idx": 49 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Provide recommendations and corrective actions for improvements.", "bbox": [ 186, 143, 778, 161 ], "page_idx": 49 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.1 Timing of Audit", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 180, 351, 200 ], "page_idx": 49 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Security audit is an on-going activity, and is not a one-off event. There are different scenarios when a security audit should be performed. The exact timing depends on your system requirements and resources.", "bbox": [ 184, 222, 875, 274 ], "page_idx": 49 }, { "type": "text", "text": "New Installation/Enhancement Audits: prior to implementation or major enhancements, in order to ensure conformance to existing policies and guidelines and meet the configuration standard.", "bbox": [ 186, 296, 816, 348 ], "page_idx": 49 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Regular Audits: conduct audits periodically, e.g. once a year, either manually or automatically using security-related tools in order to assure the minimum set of controls are implemented to detect and handle security loopholes or vulnerabilities.", "bbox": [ 186, 350, 877, 416 ], "page_idx": 49 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Sample Audits: to perform random checks in order to reflect the actual practice.", "bbox": [ 186, 420, 873, 438 ], "page_idx": 49 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Nightly or Non-Office Hour Audits: to reduce the auditing risks by performing during non-office hours or at night.", "bbox": [ 186, 442, 868, 476 ], "page_idx": 49 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.2 Auditing Tools", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 494, 339, 514 ], "page_idx": 49 }, { "type": "text", "text": "There are many automated tools which can help to find vulnerabilities. The choice of auditing tools depends on the security needs and the workload impact of monitoring.", "bbox": [ 184, 537, 863, 588 ], "page_idx": 49 }, { "type": "text", "text": "For instance, some security scanning tools can check for any existing vulnerabilities on the network (network-based) or on specific hosts (host-based) through scanning and launching simulated attacks. Results are then shown in reports for further analysis.", "bbox": [ 184, 609, 873, 677 ], "page_idx": 49 }, { "type": "text", "text": "These commercially available tools may be used together with security auditors' own developed tools. Latest tools used in the hacker community may also be used by security auditors to simulate the emerging attack activities.", "bbox": [ 184, 699, 880, 751 ], "page_idx": 49 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Manual review techniques such as social engineering attacks and auditing checklists may be applied for non-technical reviews on all levels of security awareness within the organisation.", The required time for planning depends on the nature, extent and complexity of the audit.", "bbox": [ 184, 131, 873, 183 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.3.1.1 Project Scope and Objectives", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 204, 472, 224 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Audit scope and objectives should be clearly defined and established. User requirements should be identified and agreed with security auditors before proceeding.", "bbox": [ 184, 247, 805, 299 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Examples of security audit scope are:", "bbox": [ 186, 319, 495, 337 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Internet security", "bbox": [ 186, 361, 363, 378 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• General security of an internal network", "bbox": [ 186, 381, 546, 398 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Tier 2 information systems", "bbox": [ 186, 403, 450, 419 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Hosts security", "bbox": [ 186, 424, 347, 441 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Network server's security such as web servers, email servers etc.", "bbox": [ 186, 444, 749, 461 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Network components and devices such as firewalls, routers etc.", "bbox": [ 186, 466, 742, 482 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• General security of a computer room", "bbox": [ 186, 487, 529, 504 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Network services such as directory services, mailing services, remote access services", "bbox": [ 186, 508, 847, 541 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• System documentation and records", "bbox": [ 186, 545, 514, 563 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Some audit objectives are listed below for reference:", "bbox": [ 186, 585, 620, 602 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• To ensure compliance with the system security policy and procedures with supporting evidence.", "bbox": [ 186, 626, 833, 659 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• To examine and analyse the safeguards of the system and the operational environment.", "bbox": [ 186, 663, 820, 696 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• To assess the technical and non-technical implementation of the security design.", "bbox": [ 186, 701, 877, 719 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "To validate lack of, proper or improper integration and operation of all security features.", "bbox": [ 186, 722, 870, 755 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.3.1.2 Constraints", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 778, 302, 797 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The period allowed for auditing should be adequate and sufficient enough to complete all tests. Sometimes the systems or networks have to be off-line or not in live production when performing the audit. Possible service interruption may occur. Backup and recovery of existing configuration and information must be performed before starting the security audit.", "bbox": [ 184, 820, 875, 904 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "header", "text": "Security Audit", "bbox": [ 756, 57, 880, 72 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "47", "bbox": [ 855, 942, 880, 957 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Security Risk Assessment and Audit", "bbox": [ 115, 941, 571, 958 ], "page_idx": 51 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.3.1.3 Roles and Responsibilities", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 89, 445, 109 ], "page_idx": 52 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Similar to conducting a security risk assessment, the roles and responsibilities of all parties involved should be carefully and clearly defined. Typical members involved can be referenced to \"Section 4.3.1.4. Roles and Responsibilities of Stakeholders\".", "bbox": [ 184, 131, 875, 183 ], "page_idx": 52 }, { "type": "text", "text": "In particular, the security auditors, after their appointment, should plan for pre-audit by:", "bbox": [ 184, 204, 873, 239 ], "page_idx": 52 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Identifying and verifying the current environment via documentation, interviews, meetings and manual review.", "bbox": [ 186, 261, 791, 294 ], "page_idx": 52 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Identifying the significant areas or operations that are related to the audit.", "bbox": [ 186, 299, 821, 316 ], "page_idx": 52 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Identifying the general controls that may have effects on the audit.", "bbox": [ 186, 321, 766, 337 ], "page_idx": 52 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Identifying and estimating the resources required such as the auditing tools and manpower.", "bbox": [ 186, 342, 870, 374 ], "page_idx": 52 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Identifying any special or additional processing for the audit.", "bbox": [ 186, 378, 722, 397 ], "page_idx": 52 }, { "type": "text", "text": "A security audit must be properly controlled and authorised before proceeding. A communication channel must be established between B/Ds and the security auditors.", "bbox": [ 186, 418, 877, 453 ], "page_idx": 52 }, { "type": "text", "text": "On the other hand, there are two major areas that should be considered beforehand:", "bbox": [ 186, 474, 865, 492 ], "page_idx": 52 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Independence of Security Auditors", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 186, 516, 512, 533 ], "page_idx": 52 }, { "type": "text", "text": "It is required to consider whether the appointed security auditor is appropriate for the nature of the planned security audit. An independent and trusted party should be chosen to ensure a true, fair and objective view. The hiring of internal or external security auditors should be carefully planned, especially when dealing with classified information. The selection of auditors shall ensure objectivity. Auditors shall not audit their own work.", "bbox": [ 220, 556, 882, 656 ], "page_idx": 52 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Security audit is an ongoing process in discovering and correcting security issues. Same security auditor should be avoided to be engaging for a prolonged period so as to avoid the degradation of independence as well as to avoid the blind spots of the security review due to repetitive audits with the same approaches.", "bbox": [ 221, 677, 873, 762 ], "page_idx": 52 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Staffing", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 188, 784, 297, 802 ], "page_idx": 52 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The audit should be performed by auditors with sufficient skills and experience accompanied by system administrators. Roles, responsibilities and accountabilities of each involved party should be clearly defined and assigned.", "bbox": [ 221, 825, 870, 876 ], "page_idx": 52 }, { "type": "header", "text": "Security Audit", "bbox": [ 756, 57, 880, 72 ], "page_idx": 52 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "48", "bbox": [ 855, 942, 880, 957 ], "page_idx": 52 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Security Risk Assessment and Audit", "bbox": [ 115, 941, 571, 958 ], "page_idx": 52 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.3.2 Collecting Audit Data", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 89, 403, 109 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "text", "text": "It is required to determine how much and what type of information to be captured, and how to filter, store, access and review the audit data and logs.", "bbox": [ 184, 131, 858, 166 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The amount of data collected depends on the audit scope, objectives and data availability.", "bbox": [ 184, 187, 818, 222 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Careful planning is required for data collection. Such collection shall be in accordance with the government rules and regulations, and shall not create or initiate other potential security threats and vulnerabilities. All necessary data shall be collected, properly stored and protected from unauthorised access.", "bbox": [ 184, 243, 880, 312 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Audit data can be collected and stored in different ways. For example,", "bbox": [ 186, 334, 766, 350 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Log files such as system start up and shut down information, logon and logout attempts, commands executed, access violations, accounts and password changes.", "bbox": [ 186, 374, 862, 424 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Record such as audit trails, journals, summaries, detailed reports for all transactions, statistics reports or exception reports.", "bbox": [ 186, 429, 805, 462 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Storage media such as optical disks.", "bbox": [ 186, 466, 521, 483 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Apart from electronic data collection, some physical or manual events should also be recorded and collected for future reference.", "bbox": [ 186, 505, 880, 539 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Examples are:", "bbox": [ 186, 562, 309, 580 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Computer equipment repair and maintenance activities such as date, time, supporting vendor information and the activity's description.", "bbox": [ 186, 602, 825, 637 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Change control and administration events such as configuration changes, installation of new software, data conversion or patches updating.", "bbox": [ 186, 640, 820, 674 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Physical site visits by external parties such as security auditors or guests.", "bbox": [ 186, 677, 818, 695 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Policy and procedures changes.", "bbox": [ 186, 699, 484, 717 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Operation logs.", "bbox": [ 188, 720, 354, 737 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Security incident records.", "bbox": [ 188, 741, 436, 757 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "text", "text": "In general, the audit data collection steps may follow information gathering techniques as those in a security risk assessment. However, instead of assessing the risk exposures in the environment, the objective of a security audit is to review existing security controls on operational, administrative and managerial issues, and ensure compliance to established security standards. Audit data, or evidence, is collected to support whether proper security controls are in place and enforced appropriately.", "bbox": [ 184, 781, 872, 898 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "header", "text": "Security Audit", "bbox": [ 756, 57, 880, 72 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "49", "bbox": [ 855, 942, 880, 957 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Security Risk Assessment and Audit", "bbox": [ 115, 941, 571, 958 ], "page_idx": 53 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.3.3 Performing Audit Tests", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 89, 418, 109 ], "page_idx": 54 }, { "type": "text", "text": "After thorough planning and data collection, security auditors may perform:", "bbox": [ 186, 131, 806, 149 ], "page_idx": 54 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• A general review on the existing security policies, standards or guidelines according to the defined scope of audit.", "bbox": [ 186, 173, 826, 206 ], "page_idx": 54 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• A general review on the security configurations.", "bbox": [ 186, 211, 620, 228 ], "page_idx": 54 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Technical investigation by using different automated tools for diagnostic review and/or penetration tests.", "bbox": [ 186, 231, 877, 265 ], "page_idx": 54 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Depending on the audit scope, different systems or network may be involved in a security audit. Annex C provides the purposes and coverages of different sample audit areas.", "bbox": [ 184, 292, 855, 342 ], "page_idx": 54 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.3.4 Reporting for Audit Results", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 365, 457, 385 ], "page_idx": 54 }, { "type": "text", "text": "A security audit report is required upon completion of audit work. Security auditors should analyse the auditing results and provide a report, which reflects the current security status. Performing further analysis on reports generated from scanning tools is necessary to remove non-applicable findings and false positives. The severity level may need to be adjusted in accordance with B/Ds’ environment.", "bbox": [ 184, 407, 882, 492 ], "page_idx": 54 }, { "type": "text", "text": "This audit report must be comprehensible by different readers such as IT management, executive management, related system administrators and owners, and the auditing and controlling sections.", "bbox": [ 184, 513, 877, 564 ], "page_idx": 54 }, { "type": "text", "text": "See also Annex B for the suggested contents of a security audit report.", "bbox": [ 186, 586, 764, 604 ], "page_idx": 54 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.3.5 Protecting Audit Data & Tools", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 623, 485, 642 ], "page_idx": 54 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Throughout the stages of the security audit, it is essential to safeguard the audit data and tools.", "bbox": [ 184, 664, 872, 699 ], "page_idx": 54 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Audit data and all documents relating to the audit shall be classified to an appropriate level and protected according to their classification.", "bbox": [ 186, 720, 788, 756 ], "page_idx": 54 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The auditing tools should be properly maintained, controlled and monitored to avoid misuse. Such tools should only be used by the security auditors in a controlled manner. These tools should also be removed immediately after use unless proper control has been made to protect them from unauthorised access.", "bbox": [ 184, 777, 877, 845 ], "page_idx": 54 }, { "type": "header", "text": "Security Audit", "bbox": [ 756, 57, 880, 72 ], "page_idx": 54 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "50", "bbox": [ 857, 942, 880, 958 ], "page_idx": 54 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Security Risk Assessment and Audit", "bbox": [ 115, 941, 571, 958 ], "page_idx": 54 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Security auditors shall also return all audit information to corresponding B/Ds after completing their audit services. The arrangement shall be agreed with security auditors in advance before their appointment.", "bbox": [ 184, 89, 867, 140 ], "page_idx": 55 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.3.6 Making Enhancements and Follow-up", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 162, 556, 183 ], "page_idx": 55 }, { "type": "text", "text": "If corrective actions are required, resources should be allocated to ensure that the enhancements could be performed at the earliest opportunity. Management of the system should be notified of any non-conformance. Details of follow-up can be referred in the later section.", "bbox": [ 184, 204, 855, 271 ], "page_idx": 55 }, { "type": "header", "text": "Security Audit", "bbox": [ 756, 57, 880, 72 ], "page_idx": 55 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Security Risk Assessment and Audit", "bbox": [ 117, 941, 571, 958 ], "page_idx": 55 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "51", "bbox": [ 855, 942, 878, 958 ], "page_idx": 55 }, { "type": "text", "text": "6. Service Pre-requisites & Common Activities", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 85, 638, 104 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "text", "text": "6.1 Assumptions and Limitations", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 128, 472, 147 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "text", "text": "In conducting a security risk assessment or audit, a few assumptions have been made.", "bbox": [ 184, 171, 831, 203 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• There are limited time and resources.", "bbox": [ 186, 228, 531, 244 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• It is intended to mitigate and manage security risks as comprehensive as possible.", "bbox": [ 186, 249, 813, 284 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "text", "text": "6.2 Client Responsibilities", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 305, 408, 325 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "text", "text": "When performing security risk assessment or audit by an external party, B/Ds should observe and be responsible for the following activities:", "bbox": [ 184, 348, 880, 381 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Conduct background checks and qualification checks on supporting vendor and security consultants / auditors, to ensure that they possess necessary experience and expertise.", "bbox": [ 186, 405, 872, 455 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Prepare an agreement for supporting vendor to sign, including but are not limited to the disclaimer of liability, the service details, and statement of nondisclosure, before starting any assessment or auditing activities. This is especially important when deciding to perform external penetration testing such as war dialling or hacking into the internal network from the Internet.", "bbox": [ 186, 460, 875, 542 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Assign staff to be the primary and/or secondary points of contact for the vendor.", "bbox": [ 186, 546, 875, 563 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Provide contact lists to vendor for both office and non-office hours whenever necessary.", "bbox": [ 186, 567, 857, 600 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Be cooperative and open-minded. Acknowledge the results and develop plans for improvement if there are security needs.", "bbox": [ 186, 605, 862, 638 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Allow physical and logical access only to the systems, network or computer equipment, which are necessary to perform the evaluations, and protect all assets that may be affected by this service.", "bbox": [ 186, 643, 843, 692 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Obtain formal notification from the vendor about the level of impact or damage on the network, services or systems during the testing, so that recovery scheme and appropriate incident handling procedure could be ready before proceeding.", "bbox": [ 186, 696, 872, 746 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Provide response to enquiries from security consultants / auditors within a reasonable time span.", "bbox": [ 186, 750, 830, 782 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Provide sufficient office space and office equipment for the vendor to perform their service; a restricted area is preferred.", "bbox": [ 186, 787, 863, 820 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Provide all necessary documentation about the specific area under assessment and audit such as logging policy or log review procedures, e.g. records of access log checking.", "bbox": [ 186, 825, 878, 875 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Hold regular meetings with vendor for project control and review.", "bbox": [ 186, 878, 763, 895 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "header", "text": "Services Pre-requisites & Common Activities", "bbox": [ 505, 59, 880, 74 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "52", "bbox": [ 857, 942, 880, 957 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Security Risk Assessment and Audit", "bbox": [ 115, 942, 571, 958 ], "page_idx": 56 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Apply changes or enhancements at the earliest convenience after assessing the risk involved with fallback procedure ready, especially those that were at very high risks.", "bbox": [ 186, 86, 863, 136 ], "page_idx": 57 }, { "type": "text", "text": "6.3 Service Pre-requisites", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 160, 401, 179 ], "page_idx": 57 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The following pre-requisites should be met:", "bbox": [ 186, 202, 547, 218 ], "page_idx": 57 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Provide all necessary documented information, either formal or informal, such as network diagrams, operation manual, user access control lists, security policy, standards, guidelines, and procedures. Please refer to Annex E for a sample list of documented information as supporting evidence.", "bbox": [ 186, 242, 863, 310 ], "page_idx": 57 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Provide personnel support related to the areas under study, including Internet usage, firewall configuration, network and system management, security needs and requirements, etc.", "bbox": [ 186, 313, 867, 362 ], "page_idx": 57 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Arrange guided site visit to gather more information for the assessment and audit.", "bbox": [ 186, 367, 840, 399 ], "page_idx": 57 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Choose independent third party to conduct security audit.", "bbox": [ 186, 404, 692, 422 ], "page_idx": 57 }, { "type": "text", "text": "6.4 Responsibilities of Security Consultant / Auditors", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 444, 663, 464 ], "page_idx": 57 }, { "type": "text", "text": "In performing security risk assessment or audit for a B/D, the security consultants / auditors should:", "bbox": [ 184, 487, 865, 519 ], "page_idx": 57 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Possess the necessary skills and expertise.", "bbox": [ 186, 544, 569, 561 ], "page_idx": 57 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Understand the impact of every tool and estimate impact to the B/D.", "bbox": [ 186, 564, 781, 581 ], "page_idx": 57 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Obtain proper written authorisation from other necessary parties such as Internet Service Provider (ISP) and police, especially when performing hacking tests.", "bbox": [ 186, 586, 880, 620 ], "page_idx": 57 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Document every test regardless of whether it is successful.", "bbox": [ 186, 624, 704, 640 ], "page_idx": 57 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Ensure that the report reflects B/D’s security policy and operational needs.", "bbox": [ 186, 644, 831, 661 ], "page_idx": 57 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Exercise good judgment in reporting immediately any significant security risk findings and non-conformance to the B/D.", "bbox": [ 186, 665, 862, 699 ], "page_idx": 57 }, { "type": "header", "text": "Services Pre-requisites & Common Activities", "bbox": [ 505, 59, 880, 74 ], "page_idx": 57 Follow-Up of Security Risk Assessment & Audit", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 102, 678, 122 ], "page_idx": 60 }, { "type": "text", "text": "7.1 Importance of Follow-Up", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 145, 438, 166 ], "page_idx": 60 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The benefit of security risk assessment and audit is not in the recommendations made, but in their effective implementation. When a recommendation is made, the management is basically responsible for implementing it. If management has made the decision of not implementing a recommendation, they have to bear the associated security risk and non-conformance. Adequate reasons should be provided to support the decision.", "bbox": [ 184, 187, 880, 288 ], "page_idx": 60 }, { "type": "text", "text": "There are three major areas of concern with regard to recommendations made in the security risk assessment and audit:", "bbox": [ 184, 310, 872, 344 ], "page_idx": 60 }, { "type": "image", "img_path": "images/4477a109c5618513c2b055c78c8a15c56ca3ecf523f055bd2aca7c69389bbe3d.jpg", "image_caption": [ "Figure 7.1 Follow-Up Actions on Recommendations" ], "image_footnote": [], "bbox": [ 242, 363, 840, 588 ], "page_idx": 60 }, { "type": "header", "text": "Follow-Up of Security Risk Assessment & Audit", "bbox": [ 480, 59, 885, 76 ], "page_idx": 60 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Security Risk Assessment and Audit", "bbox": [ 115, 941, 571, 958 ], "page_idx": 60 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "56", "bbox": [ 857, 942, 880, 958 ], "page_idx": 60 }, { "type": "text", "text": "7.2 Effective & Qualified Recommendations", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 91, 581, 110 ], "page_idx": 61 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Security consultants / auditors are required to produce effective and qualified recommendations, which should possess the following characteristics:", "bbox": [ 184, 134, 818, 168 ], "page_idx": 61 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Specific and clear, readily understandable and identifiable", "bbox": [ 186, 192, 699, 209 ], "page_idx": 61 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Convincing and persuasive with sufficient evidence", "bbox": [ 186, 214, 650, 230 ], "page_idx": 61 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Significant", "bbox": [ 188, 234, 321, 250 ], "page_idx": 61 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Feasible and practical", "bbox": [ 188, 254, 406, 272 ], "page_idx": 61 }, { "type": "text", "text": "In addition, the recommendations should be able to deal with the actual causes of problems, and should propose the best alternatives with supporting evidence and justifications. All these recommendations must be submitted to management which, in turn, has the authority to approve and enforce the recommendations.", "bbox": [ 184, 294, 875, 362 ], "page_idx": 61 }, { "type": "text", "text": "7.3 Commitment", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 384, 321, 403 ], "page_idx": 61 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Individual and departmental commitment is important for implementation of the recommendations. Security consultants / auditors, staff and management may have different interests, emphasis and priority given to the recommendations.", "bbox": [ 184, 426, 868, 478 ], "page_idx": 61 }, { "type": "text", "text": "7.3.1 Security Consultants / Auditors", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 500, 490, 519 ], "page_idx": 61 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Security consultants / auditors are those who first introduce the recommendations for improvement. They should:", "bbox": [ 184, 542, 880, 576 ], "page_idx": 61 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• have confidence on their recommendations and if followed, there would be desirable improvements;", "bbox": [ 186, 599, 835, 632 ], "page_idx": 61 }, { "type": "text", "text": "understand the B/D's environment and its constraints such as time, resources and culture; and", "bbox": [ 186, 637, 882, 670 ], "page_idx": 61 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• communicate through an appropriate and effective channel to give their recommendations.", "bbox": [ 186, 675, 810, 707 ], "page_idx": 61 }, { "type": "text", "text": "7.3.2 Staff", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 730, 243, 749 ], "page_idx": 61 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Staff are specifically referred to those who would be directly or indirectly affected by the recommendations. They may need to provide support for implementing the recommendations, or they are actually the users who may have to change their daily operation procedures. They should be:", "bbox": [ 184, 771, 873, 840 ], "page_idx": 61 }, { "type": "header", "text": "Follow-Up of Security Risk Assessment & Audit", "bbox": [ 480, 59, 885, 76 ], "page_idx": 61 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "57", "bbox": [ 857, 942, 880, 957 ], "page_idx": 61 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Security Risk Assessment and Audit", "bbox": [ 115, 941, 571, 958 ], "page_idx": 61 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• encouraged and motivated to co-operate with the security consultants / auditors;", "bbox": [ 184, 92, 875, 110 ], "page_idx": 62 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• given sufficient time and resources to perform the enhancements; and", "bbox": [ 186, 114, 794, 131 ], "page_idx": 62 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• assured that they would benefit from the recommendations.", "bbox": [ 186, 135, 710, 152 ], "page_idx": 62 }, { "type": "text", "text": "7.3.3 Management", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 174, 319, 195 ], "page_idx": 62 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Management plays an important role in enforcing the enhancements. They should:", "bbox": [ 184, 217, 863, 235 ], "page_idx": 62 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• be proactive rather than reactive on security matters;", "bbox": [ 184, 258, 655, 275 ], "page_idx": 62 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• provide sufficient support throughout the assessment or audit process;", "bbox": [ 186, 279, 794, 297 ], "page_idx": 62 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• allocate sufficient resources for making the enhancements;", "bbox": [ 186, 300, 705, 317 ], "page_idx": 62 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• understand that follow-up is a valuable and significant responsibility;", "bbox": [ 186, 322, 789, 338 ], "page_idx": 62 }, { "type": "text", "text": "encourage prompt enhancements with adequate planning, control and communication; and", "bbox": [ 186, 343, 791, 375 ], "page_idx": 62 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• promote staff security awareness and training.", "bbox": [ 186, 380, 603, 398 ], "page_idx": 62 }, { "type": "text", "text": "7.4 Monitoring and Follow-Up", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 439, 452, 460 ], "page_idx": 62 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Monitoring and follow-up consists of three major steps:", "bbox": [ 186, 482, 643, 500 ], "page_idx": 62 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Set up an effective monitoring and follow-up system.", "bbox": [ 186, 523, 660, 541 ], "page_idx": 62 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Identify recommendations and develop follow-up plan.", "bbox": [ 186, 544, 673, 562 ], "page_idx": 62 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Perform active monitoring and reporting.", "bbox": [ 186, 565, 563, 583 ], "page_idx": 62 }, { "type": "text", "text": "7.4.1 Set Up Monitoring and Follow-up System", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 605, 591, 625 ], "page_idx": 62 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Management should set up a monitoring and follow-up system to follow up the recommendations. Besides those responsible for the security risk assessment or audit, management may assign additional staff to oversee the overall effectiveness of the monitoring system.", "bbox": [ 184, 648, 884, 715 ], "page_idx": 62 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Management is responsible for providing adequate support, overall guidance and direction. It can establish scope, objectives and functions of the monitoring system. Areas", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 89, 526, 109 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "text", "text": "C.1 Firewall", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 134, 273, 153 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "text", "text": "This audit area is to ensure that its firewall and associated systems have been properly configured to enforce the security policy with the minimal and optimal security protection. The firewall should be audited not only for its configuration, but also for its physical access control.", "bbox": [ 184, 177, 882, 244 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "text", "text": "This audit area may cover the following:", "bbox": [ 186, 266, 522, 284 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Physical access control to the firewall host.", "bbox": [ 186, 307, 579, 324 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Firewall operating system version and patches.", "bbox": [ 186, 328, 608, 346 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Firewall configuration and controls on Internet traffic such as rulebase and ports opened.", "bbox": [ 186, 349, 878, 382 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Services permitted or disallowed to go through the firewall.", "bbox": [ 186, 386, 710, 404 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Current architecture of Internet connection such as connections with routers, proxy servers, email servers and web servers.", "bbox": [ 186, 407, 847, 441 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Connection with other third-party products for additional services such as malware detection and repair measure.", "bbox": [ 186, 445, 825, 479 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Remote connection support and configuration.", "bbox": [ 186, 482, 605, 499 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Administration and change control procedures.", "bbox": [ 186, 504, 608, 520 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Access control list, if any.", "bbox": [ 186, 525, 440, 542 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The security audit report should summarise the firewall evaluation and recommendations in the firewall architecture, configuration, administration and operation.", "bbox": [ 184, 564, 836, 615 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "text", "text": "C.2 Internal Network", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 637, 356, 656 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The goal of this audit area is to discover any vulnerability that could be exploited by authorised internal users, and to identify any weaknesses and strengths in the controls of the internal systems and networks. The topology of internal network infrastructure may be reviewed as well.", "bbox": [ 184, 680, 873, 746 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The audit test usually includes an internal network scan to check for any security holes on specified times or pre-agreed periods. The scanning on critical hosts or workstations may be included.", "bbox": [ 184, 768, 848, 820 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "75", "bbox": [ 857, 942, 880, 957 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "header", "text": "Annex C", "bbox": [ 801, 57, 880, 72 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Security Risk Assessment and Audit", "bbox": [ 115, 941, 571, 958 ], "page_idx": 79 }, { "type": "text", "text": "This audit area would likely cover:", "bbox": [ 186, 89, 477, 107 ], "page_idx": 80 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Scanning of internal workstations, servers or networks to identify hosts, services and network configuration.", "bbox": [ 186, 130, 880, 164 ], "page_idx": 80 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Identifying vulnerabilities, protocol and configuration errors on operating systems, internal firewalls, routers, network components and infrastructure.", "bbox": [ 186, 167, 838, 200 ], "page_idx": 80 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Attempting intrusion of internal network and systems.", "bbox": [ 186, 205, 667, 222 ], "page_idx": 80 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Evaluating internal security related to access control and monitoring, administration and change control procedures and practices.", "bbox": [ 186, 225, 786, 260 ], "page_idx": 80 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Recommending measures to strengthen the network security.", "bbox": [ 186, 263, 722, 281 ], "page_idx": 80 }, { "type": "text", "text": "C.3 External Network", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 323, 363, 342 ], "page_idx": 80 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The goal of this audit area is to identify security weaknesses of the systems and networks from outside such as the Internet. This helps to anticipate external attacks that might cause security breaches by scanning and launching attacks (i.e. hacking) from Internet to internal network at specified and pre-agreed time and locations.", "bbox": [ 184, 365, 870, 434 ], "page_idx": 80 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The audit area would cover:", "bbox": [ 186, 455, 420, 473 ], "page_idx": 80 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Scanning internal servers for ports and services vulnerable to attack.", "bbox": [ 186, 495, 781, 513 ], "page_idx": 80 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Scanning external network gateways to identify ports, services and topology.", "bbox": [ 186, 517, 850, 535 ], "page_idx": 80 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Attempting to gather internal configuration information from external.", "bbox": [ 186, 538, 798, 556 ], "page_idx": 80 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Launching intrusion attacks to internal systems from external.", "bbox": [ 186, 560, 729, 577 ], "page_idx": 80 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Agreements must be set up to clearly define the auditing scope and testing level details, e.g. which network segments/components or the acceptable severity of attack. The security auditor must commit to minimising disruption and avoiding damage to the systems and network.", "bbox": [ 184, 599, 847, 667 ], "page_idx": 80 }, { "type": "text", "text": "C.4 Host Security", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 705, 324, 725 ], "page_idx": 80 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The purpose of this audit area is to assess the operating system level security of different computer platforms. Misconfiguration of the operating system may open up security loopholes that may not be known by the system administrators.", "bbox": [ 184, 746, 862, 799 ], "page_idx": 80 }, { "type": "text", "text": "When considering the operating system security, accounts & password management, file system, networking workgroups, access permissions and auditing/logging are all common components that should not be omitted. "text", "text": "C.6 Remote Access", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 478, 341, 495 ], "page_idx": 82 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The audit area deals with vulnerabilities associated with remote access services via communication links such as dial-up connections and broadband connections (e.g. VPN, TLS VPN, etc.) This audit area may involve the following activities:", "bbox": [ 184, 519, 863, 570 ], "page_idx": 82 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Use automatic dialling/connection software to identify remote access users.", "bbox": [ 186, 593, 838, 611 ], "page_idx": 82 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Review security and configuration of remote access servers and the network where they are located.", "bbox": [ 186, 614, 847, 648 ], "page_idx": 82 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Conduct site visits to review the physical controls and location of modems or remote connection devices.", "bbox": [ 186, 652, 853, 684 ], "page_idx": 82 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Establish a remote access control policy or procedure.", "bbox": [ 186, 689, 665, 707 ], "page_idx": 82 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Remote access without controls may open up a backdoor to external side. The problem is how to establish a secure connection.", "bbox": [ 186, 730, 828, 763 ], "page_idx": 82 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The following may be identified and reviewed under this audit area:", "bbox": [ 186, 784, 742, 803 ], "page_idx": 82 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Applications/services requiring remote access and their security requirements.", "bbox": [ 186, 826, 860, 844 ], "page_idx": 82 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Any existing policies and procedures pertaining to remote access.", "bbox": [ 186, 847, 761, 865 ], "page_idx": 82 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Existing remote access connections such as using modems, remote access servers, modem pool connections, or broadband connections.", "bbox": [ 186, 869, 826, 902 ], "page_idx": 82 }, { "type": "header", "text": "Annex C", "bbox": [ 801, 57, 880, 72 ], "page_idx": 82 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "78", "bbox": [ 857, 942, 880, 957 ], "page_idx": 82 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Security Risk Assessment and Audit", "bbox": [ 115, 941, 571, 958 ], "page_idx": 82 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Current remote access control methods.", "bbox": [ 186, 90, 549, 107 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Current shortcomings and recommendations to improve the situation.", "bbox": [ 186, 110, 789, 128 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "C.7 Wireless Communication", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 151, 435, 170 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The audit area deals with vulnerabilities associated with wireless communication. This audit area should include, but not limited to:", "bbox": [ 184, 193, 852, 228 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Assessing Service Set Identifier (SSID) naming as well as convention and other security configurations.", "bbox": [ 186, 250, 873, 284 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Assessing current wireless encryption protocols and the strength of encryption cipher key and cipher algorithm, e.g. Wi-Fi Protected Access 3 (WPA3) supporting strong cryptography.", "bbox": [ 186, 288, 863, 338 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Assessing the adoption of Virtual Private Network.", "bbox": [ 186, 342, 643, 359 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Getting a list of access points and understanding their coverage.", "bbox": [ 186, 363, 744, 380 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Identifying any unauthorised or rogue access points.", "bbox": [ 186, 385, 653, 401 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Attempting to establish connection to the wireless communication.", "bbox": [ 186, 406, 769, 423 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Attempting to gather internal system information through the wireless communication.", "bbox": [ 186, 426, 794, 458 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Assessing if site survey is conducted and the coverage of wireless communication of the site.", "bbox": [ 186, 463, 761, 495 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Assessing if the encryption key is properly protected at the client devices.", "bbox": [ 186, 500, 825, 519 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "C.8 Phone Line", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 543, 304, 562 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The goal of the audit area is to identify undocumented or uncontrolled modems connecting internal computers directly to the telephone network. This helps to eliminate any unauthorised or inappropriate modem connection and configuration to internal network and systems.", "bbox": [ 184, 586, 875, 653 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The audit area would cover:", "bbox": [ 186, 675, 420, 693 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Assessing each modem entry point connected.", "bbox": [ 186, 717, 603, 733 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Identifying any undocumented dial-up entry points.", "bbox": [ 186, 738, 645, 755 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Attempting to establish connection to internal network.", "bbox": [ 186, 759, 675, 775 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Attempting to gather internal system information through the connection.", "bbox": [ 186, 780, 821, 797 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "79", "bbox": [ 857, 942, 880, 957 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "header", "text": "Annex C", "bbox": [ 801, 57, 880, 72 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Security Risk Assessment and Audit", "bbox": [ 115, 941, 571, 958 ], "page_idx": 83 }, { "type": "text", "text": "C.9 Web / Mobile Application", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 89, 443, 109 ], "page_idx": 84 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The audit area deals with vulnerabilities associated with web / mobile applications.
